Inverter faults (FR-A800)

The inverter's fault as the PLC reads it: the data code of 6.4 "List of fault displays" (decimal; 16 = E.OC1). The checks and remedies follow 6.5 "Causes and corrective actions" of the FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed) - the manual is the reference.

E.OC1 — Overcurrent trip during acceleration

Data code 16 (H10)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OC1
NameOvercurrent trip during acceleration
DescriptionThe output current reached about 235 % of the rated current while the motor was ACCELERATING; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. The acceleration is too sudden (on a lift: the downward acceleration time is too long).
  2. A short circuit on the output side (motor cable, motor).
  3. Pr.3 Base frequency is 60 Hz for a 50 Hz motor.
  4. The stall prevention operation level (Pr.22) is too high, or the fast-response current limit is off.
  5. Frequent regenerative driving (the output voltage above the V/F reference raises the motor current).
  6. Vector control: the RS-485 terminals' power supply is shorted; the encoder's wiring or specification (power, resolution, differential / complementary) or the motor's U, V, W wiring is wrong.
  7. Real sensorless vector control: the direction is switched between forward and reverse during torque control.
  8. The inverter and the motor capacities do not match (PM sensorless vector control).
  9. A start command was given while the motor was still coasting (PM sensorless vector control).
Corrective action
  1. Set a longer acceleration time (on a lift, a shorter downward acceleration time).
  2. If E.OC1 comes at every start: disconnect the motor and start again. Still there: contact the sales representative (the inverter).
  3. Check the output wiring: no short circuit.
  4. Set Pr.3 Base frequency to 50 Hz; set Pr.19 Base frequency voltage to the motor's rated voltage.
  5. Lower the stall prevention operation level (Pr.22) and switch the fast-response current limit on.
  6. Vector control: check the RS-485 terminal connection; wire and set the encoder and the motor to their specifications.
  7. Do not switch the direction during torque control under Real sensorless vector control.
  8. Choose an inverter and a motor of matching capacity (PM sensorless vector control).
  9. Give the start command after the motor has stopped, or use the automatic restart after instantaneous power failure / flying start (Pr.57) (PM sensorless vector control).
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.OC2 — Overcurrent trip during constant speed

Data code 17 (H11)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OC2
NameOvercurrent trip during constant speed
DescriptionThe output current reached about 235 % of the rated current at CONSTANT SPEED; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. A sudden change of the load (jammed or blocked mechanism).
  2. A short circuit on the output side.
  3. The stall prevention operation level (Pr.22) is too high, or the fast-response current limit is off.
  4. Vector control: the RS-485 terminals' power supply is shorted.
  5. Real sensorless vector control: the direction is switched during torque control.
  6. The inverter and the motor capacities do not match (PM sensorless vector control).
  7. A start command while the motor was coasting (PM sensorless vector control).
Corrective action
  1. Keep the load steady: check the mechanism for jams, the belts, the bearings.
  2. Check the output wiring: no short circuit.
  3. Lower the stall prevention operation level (Pr.22) and switch the fast-response current limit on.
  4. Vector control: check the RS-485 terminal connection.
  5. Do not switch the direction during torque control under Real sensorless vector control.
  6. Choose an inverter and a motor of matching capacity (PM sensorless vector control).
  7. Start after the motor has stopped, or use the automatic restart / flying start (Pr.57) (PM sensorless vector control).
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.OC3 — Overcurrent trip during deceleration or stop

Data code 18 (H12)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OC3
NameOvercurrent trip during deceleration or stop
DescriptionThe output current reached about 235 % of the rated current while DECELERATING or stopped; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. The speed is reduced too suddenly.
  2. A short circuit on the output side.
  3. The motor's mechanical brake closes too early (while the motor is still driven).
  4. The stall prevention operation level (Pr.22) is too high, or the fast-response current limit is off.
  5. Vector control: the RS-485 terminals' power supply is shorted.
  6. Real sensorless vector control: the direction is switched during torque control.
  7. The inverter and the motor capacities do not match, or a start command while coasting (PM sensorless vector control).
Corrective action
  1. Set a longer deceleration time.
  2. Check the output wiring: no short circuit.
  3. Check the mechanical brake's timing.
  4. Lower the stall prevention operation level (Pr.22) and switch the fast-response current limit on.
  5. Vector control: check the RS-485 terminal connection.
  6. Do not switch the direction during torque control under Real sensorless vector control.
  7. Match the capacities; start after the motor has stopped or use the automatic restart (Pr.57) (PM sensorless vector control).
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.OV1 — Regenerative overvoltage trip during acceleration

Data code 32 (H20)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OV1
NameRegenerative overvoltage trip during acceleration
DescriptionRegenerated energy or a surge on the supply raised the main circuit DC voltage to the trip level while ACCELERATING; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. The acceleration is too slow (e.g. the downward acceleration of a lift load).
  2. Pr.22 Stall prevention operation level is at or below the no-load current.
  3. Stall prevention works often on a load with a large inertia.
Corrective action
  1. Set a shorter acceleration time.
  2. Use the regeneration avoidance function (Pr.882 to Pr.886).
  3. Set Pr.22 above the no-load current.
  4. Set Pr.154 Voltage reduction selection during stall prevention operation to 10 or 11.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.OV2 — Regenerative overvoltage trip during constant speed

Data code 33 (H21)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OV2
NameRegenerative overvoltage trip during constant speed
DescriptionRegenerated energy or a surge raised the main circuit DC voltage to the trip level at CONSTANT SPEED; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. A sudden change of the load.
  2. Pr.22 Stall prevention operation level is at or below the no-load current.
  3. Stall prevention works often on a load with a large inertia.
  4. The acceleration / deceleration time is too short.
Corrective action
  1. Keep the load steady.
  2. Use the regeneration avoidance function (Pr.882 to Pr.886); use a brake unit or a power regeneration common converter (FR-CV) as needed.
  3. Set Pr.22 above the no-load current; set Pr.154 to 10 or 11.
  4. Set longer acceleration / deceleration times (under vector control a sudden acceleration may overshoot the speed and cause the overvoltage).

E.OV3 — Regenerative overvoltage trip during deceleration or stop

Data code 34 (H22)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OV3
NameRegenerative overvoltage trip during deceleration or stop
DescriptionRegenerated energy raised the main circuit DC voltage to the trip level while DECELERATING or stopped; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. The speed is reduced too suddenly.
  2. Stall prevention works often on a load with a large inertia.
Corrective action
  1. Set a longer deceleration time, to suit the load's moment of inertia; make the braking cycle longer.
  2. Use the regeneration avoidance function (Pr.882 to Pr.886).
  3. Use a brake unit or a power regeneration common converter (FR-CV) as needed.
  4. Set Pr.154 to 10 or 11.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.THT — Inverter overload trip (electronic thermal O/L relay function)

Data code 48 (H30)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.THT
NameInverter overload trip (electronic thermal O/L relay function)
DescriptionThe output transistors' temperature passed the protection level at the rated current or more, without an overcurrent trip (the inverter carries 150 % for 60 s); the output stops.
Check point
  1. The acceleration / deceleration time is too short.
  2. The torque boost (Pr.0) is too large or too small.
  3. The load pattern selection (Pr.14) does not suit the machine.
  4. The motor is overloaded.
  5. Vector control: the encoder's wiring or specification, or the motor's U, V, W wiring, is wrong.
Corrective action
  1. Set longer acceleration / deceleration times.
  2. Adjust the torque boost (Pr.0).
  3. Set the load pattern selection (Pr.14) to the machine's load.
  4. Reduce the load (check the mechanism for friction and jams).
  5. Vector control: wire and set the encoder and the motor to their specifications.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.THM — Motor overload trip (electronic thermal relay function)

Data code 49 (H31)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.THM
NameMotor overload trip (electronic thermal relay function)
DescriptionThe electronic thermal relay judged the motor overheated - overload, or poor cooling at low speed - and its accumulated heat reached the limit; the output stops. A pre-alarm (TH) shows at 85 % of the Pr.9 setting. Several motors on one inverter, or a special motor, need an external thermal relay.
Check point
  1. The motor is overloaded.
  2. Pr.71 Applied motor is not set to the motor fitted.
  3. The stall prevention operation setting does not suit the motor.
Corrective action
  1. Reduce the load (check the mechanism for friction and jams).
  2. For a constant-torque motor, set it in Pr.71.
  3. Set the stall prevention operation level correctly.
  4. Check Pr.9 Electronic thermal O/L relay against the motor's rated current.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.FIN — Heatsink overheat

Data code 64 (H40)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.FIN
NameHeatsink overheat
DescriptionThe heatsink's temperature sensor tripped; the output stops. The FIN signal can warn at about 85 % of the trip temperature (Pr.190 to Pr.196 set to 26 / 126).
Check point
  1. The ambient temperature is too high (the cabinet, its fans and filters).
  2. The heatsink is clogged.
  3. The cooling fan has stopped ("FN" on the operation panel).
Corrective action
  1. Keep the ambient temperature within the specification: check the cabinet's fans and filters.
  2. Clean the heatsink.
  3. Replace the cooling fan.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.IPF — Instantaneous power failure

Data code 80 (H50)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.IPF
NameInstantaneous power failure
DescriptionA power failure longer than 15 ms shut the output off to protect the control circuit (shorter ones are ridden through); the IPF signal is output. With a start signal ON, a failure of 100 ms or more restarts on power restoration when Pr.57 allows it.
Check point
  1. The cause of the instantaneous power failure (the supply, its contactors and fuses, loose terminals).
Corrective action
  1. Remove the cause of the power failure.
  2. Prepare a backup power supply.
  3. Set Pr.57 for the automatic restart after instantaneous power failure.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.UVT — Undervoltage

Data code 81 (H51)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.UVT
NameUndervoltage
DescriptionThe supply voltage fell to about 150 V AC (300 V AC for the 400 V class) or below, or the jumper across P/+ and P1 is missing; the output is shut off and the IPF signal is output.
Check point
  1. A large motor is started on a weak supply.
  2. The jumper across terminals P/+ and P1 is not fitted (it is removed only for a DC reactor).
Corrective action
  1. Check the supply (the transformer, the cables, the contactors). On an unstable supply the undervoltage level (the DC bus value) can be changed as the manual says.
  2. Keep the P/+ - P1 jumper fitted unless a DC reactor is connected.
  3. Still there: contact the sales representative.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.ILF — Input phase loss

Data code 82 (H52)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.ILF
NameInput phase loss
DescriptionWith Pr.872 Input phase loss protection selection = 1, one of the three input phases was lost; the output is shut off. Pr.872 = 0 (initial) switches the protection off.
Check point
  1. A broken cable, a loose terminal or a blown fuse on the three-phase input.
Corrective action
  1. Wire the input correctly; repair the broken part (cable, terminal, fuse).

E.OLT — Stall prevention stop

Data code 96 (H60)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OLT
NameStall prevention stop
DescriptionThe stall prevention held the output at 0.5 Hz for 3 s (V/F, Advanced magnetic flux vector control), or - under speed control - the torque limit held the frequency at Pr.865 Low speed detection (1.5 Hz) with the torque above Pr.874 OLT level setting (150 %) for 3 s; the output stops. "OL" shows while the stall prevention works.
Check point
  1. The motor is overloaded (blocked, jammed).
  2. The Pr.865 and Pr.874 values (V/F and Advanced magnetic flux vector control: Pr.22).
  3. Under PM sensorless vector control: is a motor connected?
Corrective action
  1. Reduce the load: free the mechanism.
  2. Change Pr.22, Pr.865 and Pr.874.
  3. For a test without a motor, select the PM sensorless vector control test operation.
  4. Remedy the stall prevention warnings OL (overcurrent) or oL (overvoltage).
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.SOT — Loss of synchronism detection

Data code 97 (H61)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.SOT
NameLoss of synchronism detection
DescriptionA PM motor lost its synchronism (PM sensorless vector control only); the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. The PM motor is overloaded.
  2. A start command was given while the motor was coasting.
  3. Is a motor connected under PM sensorless vector control? Is it an MM-CF series motor?
Corrective action
  1. Set a longer acceleration time; reduce the load.
  2. If the inverter restarts while the motor coasts: set Pr.57 (not 9999) for the automatic restart after instantaneous power failure.
  3. Check the motor's connection; for a test without a motor select the PM sensorless vector control test operation.
  4. Drive an MM-CF series IPM motor, or run the offline auto tuning for another IPM motor.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.LUP — Upper limit fault detection

Data code 98 (H62)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.LUP
NameUpper limit fault detection
DescriptionThe load passed the upper limit of the load characteristics fault detection; the output is shut off (off while Pr.1490 = 9999, the initial setting).
Check point
  1. Too much load on the machine (a jam, friction).
  2. The load characteristics settings.
Corrective action
  1. Inspect the machine.
  2. Set the load characteristics (Pr.1481 to Pr.1487) correctly.

E.BE — Brake transistor alarm detection

Data code 112 (H70)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.BE
NameBrake transistor alarm detection
DescriptionA fault in the brake circuit (e.g. a damaged brake transistor); the output is shut off. Cut the inverter's power at once. (On the separated converter types and IP55 models it means an internal circuit fault.)
Check point

  2. Is the braking duty within its rating?

E.LF — Output phase loss

Data code 129 (H81)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.LF
NameOutput phase loss
DescriptionOne of the three output phases (U, V, W) is open; the output is shut off.
Check point

  2. Is the motor much smaller than the inverter?

Corrective action

  2. Start after the motor has stopped, or use the automatic restart / flying start (PM sensorless vector control).

E.OHT — External thermal relay operation

Data code 144 (H90)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OHT
NameExternal thermal relay operation
DescriptionAn external thermal relay, or the motor's own thermal switch, opened its contact (the OH signal: "7" in one of Pr.178 to Pr.189); the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. Is the motor overheated (load, cooling fan, ambient)?
  2. Is "7" (OH signal) set in the right one of Pr.178 to Pr.189?
Corrective action
  1. Reduce the load and the operating duty.
  2. The inverter does not restart when the relay closes again by itself: reset the inverter.

Data code 145 (H91)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.PTC
NamePTC thermistor operation
DescriptionThe PTC thermistor between terminals 2 and 10 read at or above the Pr.561 level for Pr.1016's detection time; the output is shut off (off while Pr.561 = 9999).

  2. The Pr.561 and Pr.1016 settings.

E.OPT — Option fault

Data code 160 (HA0)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OPT
NameOption fault
DescriptionAn option does not agree with the settings - e.g. a torque command option missing, or a communication option fitted while the password lock (Pr.296) is 0 or 100; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. AC power wired to R/L1, S/L2, T/L3 while a high power factor converter (FR-HC2) or FR-CV is connected (Pr.30 = 2).
  2. The plug-in option selected for the torque command (Pr.804) is fitted?
  3. The vector control option and the FR-A8TP are fitted correctly; Pr.393 and Pr.862 are set right.
  4. Pr.296 is 0 or 100 while a communication option is fitted.
Corrective action
  1. Correct Pr.30 and the wiring (AC power on the converter terminals may have damaged the inverter: contact the sales representative).
  2. Fit the plug-in option and check Pr.804.
  3. Fit the vector control option and the FR-A8TP correctly; set Pr.393 and Pr.862.
  4. Set Pr.296 to another value before fitting a communication option.
  5. Return the option's manufacturer setting switch to its initial position.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.OP1 — Communication option fault

Data code 161 (HA1)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OP1  (also E.OP2, E.OP3)
NameCommunication option fault
DescriptionA communication line fault in the option in connector 1 to 3 (the number), or a fault of the FR-A8APR or its resolver wiring; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. The option's function settings.
  2. Is the plug-in option seated firmly in its connector? (FR-A800-GF: the CC-Link IE Field board on the control board.)
  3. The communication cable (broken?) and its terminating resistor.
  4. FR-A8APR only: the resolver wiring.
Corrective action
  1. Check the option's settings.
  2. Seat the option (the CC-Link IE Field board) firmly.
  3. Check the communication cable and fit the terminating resistor.
  4. Check the resolver wiring (FR-A8APR).
  5. The fault comes back after a reset: contact the sales representative.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

Data code 164 (HA4)

Operation panelE.16  (also E.17, E.18, E.19, E.20)
NameUser definition error by the PLC function

Operation panelE.PE
NameParameter storage device fault (control circuit board)
DescriptionThe stored parameters are faulty (EEPROM failure); the output is shut off.

E.CTE — Operation panel power supply short circuit / RS-485 terminals power supply short circuit

Data code 193 (HC1)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.CTE
NameOperation panel power supply short circuit / RS-485 terminals power supply short circuit
DescriptionThe power supply of the operation panel (PU connector) or of the RS-485 terminals is shorted; that output is cut.
Check point
  1. Is the PU connector cable shorted?
  2. Are the RS-485 terminals connected correctly?
Corrective action
  1. Check the PU and its cable; check the RS-485 terminals' wiring.
  2. Reset: a PU connector short with the RES signal, an RS-485 reset or by switching the power off and on; an RS-485 terminal short with the STOP/RESET key, the RES signal or the power.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.P24 — 24 V DC power fault

Data code 194 (HC2)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.P24
Name24 V DC power fault
DescriptionThe 24 V DC output of the PC terminal is shorted: the output is cut and all the external contact inputs go OFF.
Check point
  1. A short circuit on the PC terminal's output (the sensors and switches wired to it).
  2. Is an external 24 V supply at the correct voltage?
Corrective action
  1. Repair the shorted part.
  2. Supply 24 V at the correct voltage (a low input for a long time heats the internal circuit).
  3. Reset from the operation panel or by switching the power off and on - not with the RES signal.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

Data code 196 (HC4)

Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.CDO
NameAbnormal output current detection
DescriptionThe output current passed the Pr.150 Output current detection level (only with Pr.167 = 1).
Check point
  1. The Pr.150, Pr.151, Pr.166 and Pr.167 settings - and why the current is that high (the load).
Corrective action
  1. Check the load; set Pr.150, Pr.151, Pr.166 and Pr.167 as the manual describes.

Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.IOH
NameInrush current limit circuit fault
DescriptionThe inrush current limit resistor overheated; the output is shut off.
Check point
  1. Is the power switched on and off too often?
  2. FR-A840-03250 (110K) or larger: the 5 A fuse on the inrush contactor's supply - blown?
  3. Is the inrush contactor's supply circuit damaged?
Corrective action
  1. Make the circuit avoid frequent power on / off.
  2. Still there: contact the sales representative.

E.OS — Overspeed occurrence

Data code 208 (HD0)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OS
NameOverspeed occurrence
DescriptionThe motor speed passed the Pr.374 Overspeed detection level (encoder feedback, Real sensorless vector, vector, PM sensorless vector control); the output is shut off. Off in the initial setting.
Check point
  1. The Pr.374 setting.
  2. Pr.369 (Pr.851) Number of encoder pulses against the encoder fitted (encoder feedback / vector control).
Corrective action
  1. Set Pr.374 correctly.
  2. Set Pr.369 (Pr.851) correctly.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.OSD — Speed deviation excess detection

Data code 209 (HD1)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.OSD
NameSpeed deviation excess detection
DescriptionUnder vector control with Pr.285 set, the motor speed left the command (a load change) and could not be held; or the motor accelerated against a stop command (deceleration check, Pr.690).
Check point
  1. The Pr.285 and Pr.853 settings.
  2. A sudden change of the load.
  3. Pr.369 (Pr.851) against the encoder's actual pulse count.
Corrective action
  1. Set Pr.285 and Pr.853 correctly.
  2. Keep the load steady.
  3. Set Pr.369 (Pr.851) correctly.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.ECT — Signal loss detection (encoder)

Data code 210 (HD2)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.ECT
NameSignal loss detection (encoder)
DescriptionThe encoder's signal was lost under orientation, encoder feedback or vector control; the output is shut off. Off in the initial setting.
Check point
  1. The encoder signal (cable, connector).
  2. The encoder's specification.
  3. The switch on the vector control option.
  4. Is the encoder powered - not later than the inverter? Its supply voltage against its output voltage.
Corrective action
  1. Remove the cause of the signal loss; connect securely.
  2. Use an encoder that meets the specification; set the option's switch correctly.
  3. Power the encoder with the inverter. If it must come later: confirm the signal, then set Pr.376 = 0 (no signal loss detection).
  4. Match the encoder's supply voltage to its output voltage.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)

E.1 — Option fault

Data code 241 (HF1)
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.1  (also E.2, E.3)
NameOption fault
DescriptionA contact fault between the inverter and the plug-in option in connector 1 to 3 (the number), a communication option not in connector 1, or the option's manufacturer switch changed. (FR-A800-GF: also the CC-Link IE Field board's contact.)
Check point
  1. Is the plug-in option seated firmly in its connector?
  2. Excessive noise around the inverter.
  3. Is a communication option in connector 2 or 3?
Corrective action
  1. Seat the option firmly; move a communication option to connector 1.
  2. Take noise countermeasures.
  3. Return the option's manufacturer setting switch to its initial position.
  4. Still there: contact the sales representative.

E.EHR — Ethernet communication fault

Data code not in the source list - see 6.4 of the manual
Before anything else: note the code, then RESET the inverter (its STOP/RESET key, the RES signal, or the machine's alarm reset) only after the cause is found - a fault that is reset and comes back at once is still there. Work on the motor or its cable only with the inverter's power OFF and its charge lamp out (wait at least 10 minutes).
Operation panelE.EHR
NameEthernet communication fault
DescriptionThe Ethernet communication was broken for the Pr.1432 time (Pr.1431 = 3); with CC-Link IE Field Network Basic, no data within the time-out or the cyclic status bit OFF; with BACnet/IP, another inverter's IP address inside the command source range.
Check point
  1. The Ethernet board and cable; is Pr.1432 too short?
  2. Excessive noise around the inverter.
  3. CC-Link IE Field Basic: the master's time-out and the own station's cyclic status bit.
  4. BACnet/IP: other inverters' IP addresses in the command source range.
Corrective action
  1. Fit the board; connect (replace) the cable; set Pr.1432 longer.
  2. Against noise: change the master's communication settings (time-out, retries).
  3. CC-Link IE Field Basic: set a longer time-out; turn the own station's cyclic status bit ON.
  4. BACnet/IP: keep other inverters' IP addresses out of the command source range.
FR-A800 Instruction Manual (Detailed), IB-0600503ENG, 6.5 Causes and corrective actions - the manual (a copy put in the Help folder as FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf opens from there: FR-A800_Instruction_Manual.pdf)
